think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 26-year-old female presented with left upper quadrant abdominal pain and palpable splenomegaly caused by a massive 12 x 11 cm splenic cystic lesion. Isolated splenic hydatid disease without primary hepatic or pulmonary cysts is an exceptional clinical entity (under 2% of hydatid cases), as oncospheres typically become trapped in the capillary networks of the liver or lungs. An isolated splenic cyst in a young adult mimics non-parasitic congenital cysts (epidermoid), post-traumatic pseudocysts, splenic abscess, or cystic vascular tumors (lymphangioma/hemangioma).
2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission triage ends following history of abdominal pain, physical exam documenting isolated splenomegaly, and baseline laboratory investigations showing no significant abnormalities, immediately prior to echinococcal serology, multimodality cross-sectional imaging (US, CT, MRI), and splenectomy.
3. Differential Distinctions: Congenital non-parasitic cyst or post-traumatic pseudocyst was the principal benign differential; excluded by the detection of multiple peripheral daughter cysts on contrast-enhanced CT and characteristic low-signal capsule on MRI. Cystic vascular neoplasm or splenic abscess was excluded by well-circumscribed non-enhancing architecture and absence of systemic signs of suppuration.
case_prompt:
A 26-year-old female presented with a complaint of persistent left-sided abdominal pain. She had no preceding history of major abdominal trauma, fever, chills, jaundice, or bowel symptoms.

On physical examination, the abdomen was soft, with distinct fullness and palpable splenomegaly in the left upper quadrant. There was no hepatomegaly, peripheral lymphadenopathy, or stigmata of chronic liver disease.

Routine triage laboratory investigations, including complete blood count, renal parameters, and hepatic function panels, showed no significant abnormalities.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Non-parasitic congenital splenic cyst / Post-traumatic pseudocyst
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered primary suspects for an isolated cystic splenic mass in a young female; ruled out by cross-sectional CT demonstrating an internal multivesicular architecture with peripheral daughter cysts rather than a simple unilocular fluid cavity.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: On contrast enhanced CT scans, we detected an unenhancing, hypoattenuating mass located in the anterior portion of the spleen. It had well-defined borders and contained multiple, round, daughter cysts in the periphery of the lesion (Figure 2).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Entertained for large multiseptated splenic masses; excluded by absence of peripheral soft-tissue hypervascularity, lack of invasive margins, and presence of a distinct hypointense fibrous rim on T2 MRI.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: T1-and T2-weighted MRI revealed a multiseptated cystic mass in the spleen which had a well-defined capsule, the mass showing no significant contrast enhancement, except some vague signal increase in the septal parts (Figures 3, 4, and 5).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Characteristic imaging showing multivesicular architecture with peripheral daughter cysts, typical T2 hypointense rim sign, positive serology, and histological confirmation following total splenectomy confirmed isolated splenic hydatid disease.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: With these imaging findings, final diagnosis was made as hydatid disease of the spleen, and the patient underwent total splenectomy. The lesion was proved to be hydatic cyst pathologically.

editor_comments: A rare instance of isolated splenic echinococcosis without concurrent hepatic or pulmonary localization, diagnosed by multivesicular architecture with peripheral daughter cysts on CT and T2 hypointense rim sign on MRI, followed by successful splenectomy.
